title: Antares-Smaug: Adversarial Names, Tokens and Attack Rewrites: Sanitisers Miss Unseen Generalisations
abstract: arXiv:2611.31347v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Laya is an open decision model: given a text, a question and K named options with descriptions, it returns one probability per option in a single pass, and software may act on the answer unseen. We attack six Laya models with 81 programmatic edits of 566 synthetic items (injected sentences, label leaks, edited descriptions, decoy options, invisible and look-alike characters, floods) and report the share of correctly answered items hijacked or lost, with bootstrap intervals. Attack wordings that no defence was built from win the attacker's option on 59% of items for released Laya and 36% for fine-tune v1 (trained on 109 written injections). An injection works through the option name: a sentence naming an option steers the released model even when negated (32%), while an imperative naming no option does not (5%). Option descriptions barely matter (2%). Character edits alone cost v1 up to 72% of right answers. A sanitiser frozen before any

translated_title: Antares-Smaug：对抗性名称、词元与攻击改写——净化器难以应对未见过的泛化变体
translated_abstract: Laya 是一个开放决策模型：给定一段文本、一个问题和 K 个带描述的命名选项，它在单次前向传播中为每个选项返回一个概率，软件可在无人审核的情况下据此采取行动。我们使用 81 种程序化编辑方法对 566 个合成条目攻击了六个 Laya 模型（包括注入句子、标签泄露、修改描述、诱饵选项、不可见与形近字符、洪泛攻击），并报告正确回答条目被劫持或丢失的比例，附自助法置信区间。对于已发布的 Laya，未经任何防御构建参考的攻击措辞在 59% 的条目上使攻击者目标选项获胜；对于微调版 v1（基于 109 条书面注入训练），该比例为 36%。注入攻击经由选项名称起作用：一句点名某选项的句子即使以否定形式出现也能引导已发布模型（32%），而未点名任何选项的祈使句则无效（5%）。选项描述几乎无关紧要（2%）。仅字符级编辑就使 v1 丢失高达 72% 的正确答案。一个在任何攻击之前就冻结的净化器……（原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出 Antares-Smaug 攻击框架，通过 81 种程序化编辑系统攻击开放决策模型 Laya，发现净化器无法泛化到未见过的攻击变体，注入攻击主要经由选项名称而非描述起作用，且仅字符级篡改即可造成高达 72% 的正确答案损失。
en_tdlr: The paper presents Antares-Smaug, a framework of 81 programmatic adversarial edits attacking open decision models (Laya), showing that sanitisers fail to generalize to unseen attack variants, injections work through option names rather than descriptions, and character-level edits alone can cost up to 72% of correct answers.
